thread:
Maria Chen: Quick handoff — I'm logging out in 10. Primary for the next 6h is @Alex G, secondary @Priya Nair. I'm leaving notes below for anything that pops. :wave:

Alex G: Got it, thanks Maria. Any running customer-facing work we should be aware of?

Maria Chen: Two things: 1) We have a rolling 4xx spike against /v1/generate from a single IP block (started ~05:10 UTC) — mitigated by temporary rate-limiting rule but still noisy. 2) A Dedicated pool host shows elevated GPU mem pressure on node dpool-03 — not yet service impacting.

incident-bot: [ALERT] 05:12 UTC - 4xx-rate-spike on /v1/generate (service: api-prod). Severity: P2. Incident channel: #incidents. Pager: primary.

Priya Nair: I'm on standby as secondary. For the 4xx spike, do we want to open a short-lived CIDR block blackhole or start stricter throttling by API key?

Sam (SRE): If it's a single IP block with lots of unauth traffic, prefer CIDR block at edge for now (less risk of collateral for legit users). But confirm there are no legitimate customers from that ASN. Runbook link: https://runbooks.internal/redwood/api-rate-spike

Jamie: Tagging customer-success: if we blackhole a CIDR and a legit partner sits behind it we need rapid rollback. Who can check the ASN mapping quickly?

Alex G: I'll check ASN and recent request headers. If it's clearly abusive, I'll apply an edge ACL for 15m and escalate to DDoS if it persists.

Maria Chen: Node dpool-03 memory pressure — root cause unclear. Logs show repeated kernel OOM-killer events on worker container process lm-infer-1 around 04:50-05:00. I restarted the service once and pressure dropped but autoscaler bumped more hosts. Not affecting request success yet but latency tail could degrade. Runbook: https://runbooks.internal/redwood/gpu-mem-pressure

incident-bot: [INCIDENT] 05:25 UTC - Incident created (id: INC-2026-042). Affected: Dedicated pool dpool-03. Oncall: Alex G (primary), Priya Nair (secondary).

Alex G: For escalation rules — let's reiterate: P0 = pager to phone + text to primary + page secondary if no ack in 2m. P1 = slack page to #eng-oncall and DM to primary, escalate to secondary if no response in 10m. P2 = slack thread and async notes.

Priya Nair: Agree. Also adding nuance for Dedicated: if a Dedicated pool loses >30% capacity in a region -> auto-escalate to infra lead (Sam) immediately.

Sam (SRE): Confirmed. I'll add a watch on the autoscaler metrics and a static alert: autoscaler_down_pct > 30% for 3m triggers phone page to infra lead.

Jamie: Handoff checklist reminder (quick):
- Primary/secondary confirmed (yes)
- Active incidents noted (INC-2026-042)
- Customers to notify? (none yet)
- Runbooks linked and accessible (yes)
- Pager routing verified (yes)

Maria Chen: Couple of practical steps before I go:
1) I left a short eval prompt set called "latency-smoke-05" in /sre/handoffs/ for you to kick if tail rises.
2) If you need to escalate to product for a customer-impacting route change we need PM approval — ping @Jamie.

Alex G: Thanks — I'll: 1) check ASN, 2) apply edge ACL for 15m if abusive, 3) monitor dpool-03 and run the smoke set every 10m for next hour. If tail P99 > 800ms for 3 consecutive runs -> escalate to P1.

Priya Nair: If Alex doesn't ack the page for P0, I will take over after 2m and start mitigation. I can also roll a hotfix for the worker container if dpool-03 shows repeat OOMs.

incident-bot: [REMINDER] 05:40 UTC - Handoff check: primary acked. Auto-escalation window active for 2m.

Sam (SRE): One more ops suggestion — if you apply an edge ACL, include an explicit rollback command snippet in the Slack thread like:
```bash
# add temporary block
curl -X POST https://edge-api/internal/acl -d '{"cidr":"1.2.3.0/24","duration":15}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $EDGE_TOKEN'
# rollback
curl -X DELETE https://edge-api/internal/acl/1.2.3.0/24 -H 'Authorization: Bearer $EDGE_TOKEN'
```

Alex G: Copying that into my notes. I'll add action timestamps when I run them.

Jamie: If this becomes customer impacting, template for customer notice is in /templates/incident_customer_notify.md — keep it short and include mitigation steps + ETA.

Maria Chen: Thanks team, logging off now. Good luck, ping me on phone if anything P0. :lock: :rocket:

Alex G: Acknowledged. Taking over primary now.

Priya Nair: Standing by as secondary.

incident-bot: [CLOSE LOOP] 05:50 UTC - Primary change recorded (new primary: Alex G, previous: Maria Chen). Thread pinned to #eng-oncall for 24h.
